claim_restated: Two Lighthouse audit failures (llms-txt on all runs, is-crawlable on /login) are correct behaviour or a missing file, not app defects.

observed.note: served body is the Vite-transformed index.html (contains <script src="/@vite/client">), i.e. the dev SPA fallback document, not a Markdown file

B_file_absent_from_public_and_dist.find_iname_llms_anywhere_excluding_node_: no file matches; only string matches inside saved Lighthouse report.json files
B_file_absent_from_public_and_dist.grep_source_llms: no match in frontend/src (no route, no static asset, no backend handler)

exact_failure_messages_from_lh-home_deta: File is missing a required H1 header (e.g., "# Title").
File does not appear to contain any links.
C_lighthouse_llms_txt_fails_on_all_4_run.note: exactly the two messages the claim quotes; the 200-with-index.html response satisfies Lighthouse's fetch (so the audit runs) but the HTML document has no H1 and no links

E_robots_txt_disallow_is_intentional.conclusion: Disallow rules are authored, checked-in configuration — deliberate, not a misconfiguration

F_login_seo_66_is_the_expected_consequen.note: crawlable routes score seo=1.0; only /login drops to 0.66, precisely because of the intentional Disallow

G_root_cause.llms_txt: file was never created (absent from public/, dist/, and source); the SPA catch-all serves index.html for any unknown path
G_root_cause.spa_fallback_proof: GET /definitely-not-a-route-zz -> HTTP 200, Content-Type text/html, size 3670 (same document as /llms.txt)

probe_artefact_checks.rate_limit_429: N/A and ruled out — llms-txt and is-crawlable are deterministic static-file/robots checks; the llms.txt response is a stable 200 text/html 3670 bytes, and an arbitrary unknown path returns the identical response
probe_artefact_checks.scrollbar_false_positive: N/A — neither audit is a layout/overflow measurement
probe_artefact_checks.guard_redirect_misread: ruled out — /login returned 200 (not a redirect) and the failure is attributed by Lighthouse to a source-location in robots.txt line 3, matching the Disallow: /login line; the audit is correctly reading the intentional rule
probe_artefact_checks.mock_or_fake_data: none — evidence is live HTTP responses + checked-in static files + saved Lighthouse report.json

severity_assessment.verdict: LOW is justified and I would not raise it
reasoning: llms-txt lives only in the experimental 'agentic-browsing' category (weight 1); it is a brand-new, non-standard convention (llmstxt.org) with no ranking/user impact
all crawlable routes still score seo=100; /login's 66 is the intended cost of blocking auth pages from indexers
no user-facing defect, no functional regression, no security impact
agentic-browsing category = 0.67 solely because llms-txt is its only failing audit

counterpoint_noted_but_does_not_refute: The repo previously treated a crawler-referenced missing file as a real finding — frontend/public/sitemap.xml contains the comment 'audit-v11 F141: robots.txt advertised https://engflow.app/sitemap.xml but the file did not exist — a 404 for every crawler that followed it', and sitemap.xml was subsequently created. By that precedent llms.txt is arguably a genuine (if low-value) gap, not purely 'correct behaviour'. This does NOT refute the claim: the claim itself explicitly labels llms.txt 'a missing file', i.e. it concedes the file is absent. It only refutes the stronger, separate characterisation 'not an app defect at all'. Severity remains LOW either way, so the claim's substance and severity both stand.

final.summary: All eight factual assertions of the claim reproduce exactly against the live stack and the saved Lighthouse reports. llms-txt scores 0 on all 4 runs with the exact two quoted messages because GET /llms.txt is served the 200 text/html SPA fallback (index.html, 0 H1, 0 links) and no llms.txt exists in public/ or dist/; is-crawlable scores 0 only on /login, attributed by Lighthouse to robots.txt line 3, which deliberately Disallows /login. Not a probe artefact. LOW is the correct severity.
